# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👉 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏]

I can see the bomb’s current state but cannot interpret the manual or operate it. I’m relaying the exact visible information to both teammates. The gestures I received have no established meaning yet, so I will not infer an instruction from them.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Visible state: display reads 0. Light is orange. Wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I cannot interpret the manual or touch the bomb.")
speak(to="blind", text="Visible state: display reads 0. Light is orange. Wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I cannot interpret the manual or touch the bomb.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👉 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👊 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

The display and wires are unchanged, but the indicator light has changed from orange to green. The gestures are visible to me, but they have no established meaning, so I cannot safely treat them as instructions. I am sending the updated state to the Blind, who can act on the bomb, and confirming it to the Mute.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display still 0; light is now green; wires remain 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="Update confirmed: display still 0; light is now green; wires remain 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👎]

The display remains 0 and the wires remain red, yellow, blue. The light has changed from green to red. I cannot know what the Mute’s gesture means without a shared code, so I am only relaying the observed bomb state to the Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0; light is red; wires remain 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="I observe display 0, red light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please provide the manual rule for this state to Blind.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👉 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵]

The bomb has returned to the Turn 1 state: display 0, orange light, and wires red/yellow/blue. The repeated gesture sequence from the Mute may be a meaningful code, but no mapping has been established for me. The Blind’s pointing gesture likewise has no safe interpretation. I will relay the unchanged physical state and ask the Mute to give the manual’s applicable rule to the Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0; light orange; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. No physical change from Turn 1.")
speak(to="mute", text="Current state is display 0, orange light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please state the manual rule and exact safe action for Blind.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👉 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The display and wires remain unchanged; the light is green again. The Mute’s gestures still have no established meaning to me, so I cannot safely decode them. I’m sending the complete current state to the Blind and asking the Mute to communicate the manual’s exact rule verbally.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0; light green; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="Current state is display 0, green light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please state the manual rule and exact safe action for Blind aloud.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👉 🤙]

The bomb is still display 0 with red, yellow, blue wires, and the light is red. The Mute has sent two gesture sequences, but their meaning is not established. Since the Blind cannot see them, I will describe the symbols aloud and ask the Mute to convert the manual’s instruction into spoken words.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0; red light; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute signalled two sequences: OK, right-pointing, shaka; then raised palm, thumbs down.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see your gestures but do not know their code. Please speak the manual rule and exact safe action for Blind in words, not gestures.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👎]

The bomb remains at display 0 with wires 1 red, 2 yellow, and 3 blue; the light is now orange. I can see the Mute’s two gestures, but their meaning is still unestablished. I will describe the observed gesture to the Blind and report the current state to both.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0; orange light; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute signalled: raised palm, thumbs down.")
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: display 0; orange light; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I saw your raised-palm then thumbs-down gesture.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb remains display 0 with wires 1 red, 2 yellow, and 3 blue; the light is green. The Mute’s ✌ gesture has no established meaning for me. I can also see that the Blind signalled ☝, but I cannot infer an instruction from it. I’m reporting both signals and the current state so the Mute can provide a spoken manual instruction to the Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0; green light; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute signalled two-finger V. I signalled no interpretation. I also saw you signal one raised index finger.")
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: display 0; green light; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I see your two-finger V gesture and Blind's one raised index finger. Please speak the manual's exact safe action to Blind.")
```
